A109381_sparse: for all B, k >= 1 there is K with #{n < X : a(n) <= B}^k <= K X^2 (factorial digits of N < m! determine N, so <= (B+1)^m such N; c^j <= c^c j!); A109381_density_zero: a(n) -> infinity on a density-1 set. conjecture_implies_brocard_finite: the conjecture implies finitely many solutions of n^2 = k! + 1 (such n have a(n) <= 1), so it is at least as hard as Brocard's problem. Outside Lean: the computation that a(n) <= 1 with n^2 < 31! holds exactly for n in {0,1,3,5,11,12,27,29,71,72,213,215,603,635,1917,1183893} (certificate/lowdig.c).
